newsitem.title: USA: Democrats' panel to weigh campaign finance reform.
newsitem.headline: Democrats' panel to weigh campaign finance reform.

text.p: The Democratic Party is to set up a special panel to review financial contributions, its general chairman, Sen. Christopher Dodd, said on Wednesday.

Dodd made the announcement in a speech at the National Press Club in the midst of a controversy over reports that possibly illegal foreign contributions had been made to President Bill Clinton's election campaign.

Dodd said details would be provided soon by party national chairman Don Fowler. He also suggested that rather than waiting to complete the lengthy process of changing campaign finance laws, the two major political parties should act immediately to stop contributions from non-U.S. citizens and end so-called soft money contributions.

U.S. residents, even if they are not citizens, are allowed to give money. The furore over campaign contributions stemmed partly from the disclosure that an Indonesian couple residing in the United States gave $425,000 to the Clinton campaign.
Clinton responded with a speech calling for campaign finance reform.
Soft money is cash given to the parties by interest groups that is not subject to campaign finance limitations. The money is then used to help political candidates.

"If there is agreement between the two parties ... we ought to stop contributions from non-U.S. citizens and we ought to end soft money," Dodd said. "It seems to me the two major parties in this country ought to be able to make that commitment to each other and the American public and then work out the details of how to do it," he said.
